annotation.title_clean: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on 'Proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)'
annotation.title_en: Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee on the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability Directive)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 140
annotation.summary_en: EESC opinion welcoming the Commission's proposed AI Liability Directive, with its presumption of causality and access to evidence. It urges clear definitions, uniform application, alternative dispute resolution, insurance monitoring, and a review after three years. It briefly addresses autonomous vehicle insurance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Supports the rebuttable presumption of causality and the right of access to evidence for high-risk AI.
Calls for clear legal definitions and the most uniform liability scheme possible across the EU.
Advocates free, mandatory alternative dispute resolution schemes with EU-wide coordination.
Asks the Commission to monitor insurance and incidents before considering strict liability or mandatory insurance.
Recommends reviewing the directive 3 years after entry into force, not 5.
